node.statement: Fix U in calU and B in icalH. Exact unitality and U^dagger bold-dot U=J give f_U(0)=0, so uniqueness forces g_U(0)=0. For all sufficiently small real t, set X_B(t)=U bold-dot (J+tB+g_U(tB)). The defining zero equation is exactly X_B(t)^dagger bold-dot X_B(t)=J because the involution reverses the product, and the preceding step gives the required right inverse, so X_B(t) lies in calU and X_B(0)=U. Differentiating at zero gives dX_B/dt at zero = L_U(B+Dg_U(0)B). Hence im L_U(I+Dg_U(0)) is contained in T_U calU.
